content.text:
`addMonths` now clamps the day to the target month's last day, so Jan 31 + 1 month gives Feb 28 instead of Mar 3.

The change is in `dates.js`. It moves the date to the 1st before `setMonth`, so the month change can't overflow. It then clamps the original day to the length of the target month. Time of day is kept and the input date is not mutated.

Checks I ran:
- Jan 31 + 1 → Feb 28 (2026) and Feb 29 (2024 leap year)
- Mar 31 + 1 → Apr 30
- Jan 31 + 12 → Jan 31 2027
- Mar 31 − 1 → Feb 28
- Feb 29 2024 + 12 → Feb 28 2025
- Jan 15 + 1 → Feb 15 (non-edge case unchanged)
- Time of day preserved and input not mutated

Notes:
- `npm test` is `node --test`, but the project has no test files, so it doesn't verify this fix. I didn't add tests. If you want, I can add a `dates.test.js` with these cases.
- The fix covers the month-end overflow. If billing code computes the billing date some other way, it may need the same treatment. I only looked at `dates.js`.
- The clamping uses local time, the same as the original `setMonth`. If billing runs in UTC on a server with a different local zone, that's worth checking.
